To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we identified 3 new phosphorylated isoforms of αs-CN in bovine milk and that we showed the existence of at least 2 independent regulatory mechanisms for phosphorylation of caseins in the mammary gland.
we identified 3 new phosphorylated isoforms of αs2-casein and that the variation of phosphorylation isoforms in αS-CN suggests different phosphorylation pathways.

the relative concentration of each αS-casein isoform varies considerably among individual cows and that the phenotypic and genetic correlations between isoforms suggest at least 4 different phosphorylation pathways.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the variation in phosphorylated forms of caseins and the relationships between them.
the variation in phosphorylated forms of αS-CN and their relationships in milk of individual cows.
the first comprehensive study on the phosphorylation degree of CN in individual cow milk.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
αS-CN phosphorylates in a complex and intricate way, and this process is influenced by multiple factors.

there are 2 different regulatory systems responsible for the phosphorylation of αs-CN, one responsible for the phosphorylated isoforms of αs1-CN and αs2-CN with lower levels of phosphate groups (8 to 12 phosphate groups), and another responsible of the phosphorylation isoforms with higher phosphate group content (13 to 15 phosphate groups) of αs2-CN.
the phosphorylation degree of CN is a quantitative trait with a high genetic variability, and that the genetic background of CN phosphorylation is a complex trait with different regulatory systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the relationships among bovine casein phosphorylation isoform concentrations suggest that there may be different phosphorylation pathways in bovine milk.
the variation in phosphoryl degree among different isoforms of αs-CN suggests the existence of different phosphorylation pathways in the mammary gland.

the phosphorylation isoforms αS2-CN with higher level of phosphorylation (12 to 15 phosphorylation sites) were more closely related to the isoforms αS-CN with lower level of phosphorylation than to other isoforms with the same level of phosphorylation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relationships among bovine casein phosphorylation isoform suggest different phosphorylation mechanisms.

the phosphorylation of α-casein is highly variable in the population, suggesting that the phosphorylation degree of casein is an individual characteristic that can be selected for in breeding programs to improve the technological properties of milk.
the relationships among αS-CN phosphoryl isoforms may be used as a tool to investigate the mechanisms of CN phosphorylation.
